# Fabulae, selected teaching translation

## Identity and consulted witness

Hyginus, Fabulae 164, trans. Roger T. Macfarlane, BYU OGCMA teaching witness. [Selected digital carrier](https://cal.byu.edu/macfarlane/OGCMA/AthenaANCIENT_Hyginus.htm). Accessed and saved 8 September 2026. The raw response is retained at `working/sources-texts-references/primary-texts/attica/hyginus-fabulae-macfarlane-digital.html` (SHA-256 `b6dde32c66b1693bd9e72417e54351cc711eda445d09516e93fdb036097d047a`). A saved page can contain more material than the selected reading; no whole-work reading is claimed.

## Source-specific reading

Fabula 164 makes Jupiter the appointed judge. Minerva’s first olive wins the competition, Neptune intends inundation, and Mercury prevents it at Jupiter’s command. Minerva subsequently founds Athens under her own name; the entry calls it the first town established there. The restraining intervention gives the aftermath a different operation from Pseudo-Apollodorus’s accomplished flood.

The BYU page explicitly credits Macfarlane’s translation. Its Latin column contains entries 142, 165 and 168, not 164. The separate Lateinlex display of 164.1–3 supports the reading of prevented inundation; its editorial metadata has not been established. The BYU note concerning PHI and Marshall’s 2002 edition must not be used to claim a parallel Latin collation of its absent entry 164.
